title: Prospective Registry for the Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes Following Hip-Preserving Surgery
summary:
Background: Diseases and misalignments of the hip joint can cause pain and limited mobility. Surgery is intended to help preserve the patient’s natural hip joint for as long as possible.
Research Question: This study examines how pain, mobility, and quality of life evolve after surgery and which factors influence the treatment outcome.
Methodology: Adult patients are examined and interviewed before surgery and at six weeks, three months, and twelve months afterward. In addition, data on routine care, potential complications, and, if applicable, a subsequent hip replacement are collected. The study does not alter the treatment itself.
conditions: Femoroacetabular Impingement and Hip Dysplasia in Adults Scheduled for Hip-Preserving Surgery.
Other specified joint disorders, not elsewhere classified: pelvic region and thigh [pelvis, femur, buttock, hip, hip joint, sacroiliac joint]

interventions.name:
Patients who have undergone hip-preserving surgery
Prospective, non-interventional observation of patients aged 18 and older diagnosed with femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and/or hip dysplasia who undergo hip-preserving surgery at the University Clinic for Orthopedics at Pius Hospital Oldenburg.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Age 18 or older
-Diagnosed femoroacetabular impingement (hip impingement) and/or hip dysplasia (malformation of the hip socket)
-Planned or completed hip-preserving surgery at Pius Hospital in Oldenburg
-Capacity to give informed consent and willingness to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
-Belonging to a patient group that is particularly vulnerable
-Language barrier that prevents adequate informed consent or participation
-Inability to give informed consent
